html:
The Battle of Uhud was fought in March 625 at the foot of Mount Uhud, just outside Medina, between the Muslims under Muhammad and a quraysh army from Mecca that came for revenge after Badr.

The Muslims at first had the upper hand. Then archers posted on a hill left their places to take part in the plunder, and the Meccan cavalry struck from behind. Many Muslims were killed, Muhammad was wounded, and the Meccans withdrew without taking Medina. The result was a setback, not a rout, and it taught the Muslims about discipline. It was followed by the Battle of the Trench in 627.
